text: Hi po! We're Ruel Mendio and Benedict Paul Samson from Assumption College of Davao. This is Aumazing — a gamified learning app for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder, built around each child's own skill level rather than their age.
These are BPS and Reiz. They guide the child through every activity in the app — and they'll walk you through this presentation too.
In Davao City, one therapy session costs seven to eight hundred pesos. A child who needs three hours a day can cost a family over forty thousand pesos a month.
The city's public intervention center offers therapy for free — but it serves around one thousand one hundred sixty clients, so many families end up waiting.
And early intervention only works with daily repetition. Between clinic visits, that falls on the parents — usually the mother. Without proper tools, she's guessing which activity to do today.

Aumazing replaces that guesswork. The child plays a short gamified pre-assessment, and an AI model turns how they play — accuracy, response time, retries — into a skill level for communication, social, and play.
From that, it recommends which modules to do next. A post-assessment then shows the parent what actually changed. No worksheets. No guessing.
Aumazing works today — the games, the assessment, the dashboard, and offline mode all run on a real device.
Next we're testing with parents and children here in Davao, and coordinating with therapy centers so the directory reflects what's really available.
If you're a parent, a therapist, or a center, we'd like your feedback. Ang goal namin is simple: that a parent at home knows exactly what to do next with their child. Thank you po for watching.
